L1 next-sound.notes: English matches Dafny: Next(after) is strictly after `after` and is an occurrence (anchor plus whole periods, or the once-time). Non-vacuous: Interval(0,1000), after=0 gives 1000. Matches schedule.before.ts nextOccurrence for both kinds.

L2 next-minimal.notes: English matches Dafny: any real occurrence x > after yields a Some no later than x. Non-vacuous: Once(10), after=5, x=10. Matches the TS (floor-based interval arithmetic and once comparison).

L3 next-none.notes: English matches Dafny: None iff Once with at <= after; intervals always have a next. Non-vacuous: Once(5), after=10 gives None, as the TS does. Redundant with L1+L2 but it is the readable exact-results statement; keep.

L4 first-interval.notes: English matches Dafny: First is a real occurrence >= now and no real occurrence >= now is earlier. First is the anchor when now <= anchor, else Next(now-1), which is the TS rule (anchor >= now ? anchor : next(now-1)). The bounds (now - 1 stays in range) are proven.

L5 classify-not-due.notes: English matches Dafny: nxt > now gives only the stored next, unchanged, with nothing dispatched or skipped. Non-vacuous: Once(10), nxt=10, now=5. Matches the TS early return for once and interval.

L6 classify-due.notes: English matches Dafny: exactly one of dispatch/skip, chosen by policy; the acted-on occurrence is the Witness (latest due); the new next is Next(now) for intervals and none for once, strictly after now. Matches the TS for both policies and both kinds. Premise A2 (nxt is an occurrence) is a shell precondition, see general. The English does not say that earlier missed interval occurrences are dropped without a record; the TS does the same, so this is clarity, not a defect.

L7 first-once.notes: English matches Dafny: First(Once(at)) == Some(at) even when at is in the past. Non-vacuous: at=0, now=0. Matches the TS (firstOccurrence returns the once-time regardless of now).

L8 first-after-occurrence.notes: English matches Dafny: creating at a+k*e+1 yields a+(k+1)*e, a past occurrence is not counted. Non-vacuous: a=0, e=1000, k=0, now=1 gives 1000. Matches the TS (nextOccurrence(now-1)). Not implied by L4 alone because now is not an occurrence; kept as an exact-result law.

general: Tier high-stakes confirmed: the block decides when automation runs dispatch or skip. No accepted mutants (mutate.json accepted is empty); none to agree or disagree with. Proof: `dafny verify --verify-included-files blocks/schedule/occurrence/Block.dfy` with the pinned lab toolchain gives 49 verified, 0 errors; there is no assume, axiom, verify-false or extern in Occurrence.dfy or Block.dfy. Range: every shell input I traced is inside the bounds. Gateway timestamps are years 0000-9999 (about 6.2e13 to 2.5e14 ms, inside LIMIT 2^50 ~ 1.1e15 ms); interval periods are 60 to 31536000 s (under LIMIT); the façade checks Wf and InRange and throws on a non-safe integer before every call; intermediates stay below 2^52, inside the safe range. Missing law kinds: progress and recovery are n/a for pure functions; uncertain-outcomes is n/a (no effects). Stale-inputs is n/a only because of A2. World-model gap: A2 (the stored next is an occurrence of the current trigger) is the sole precondition of L6 and is what keeps a stale record from producing a non-occurrence dispatch. The shell supports it (scheduler classifies only enabled automations; replace recomputes while enabled; enable recomputes unless a retained automatic run carries an identical trigger, in which case the stored occurrence was computed for that same trigger). I found no gateway test that exercises that path, so A2 needs its contract test (already required by the packet) before cut-over. A non-occurrence stored next is not a law the block can state without a product decision on what it should do, so this is a maintainer item rather than a REJECT. Calendar triggers are out of scope of this block.
